answer: A concrete sybil defense: make identity costly in the physical world, not just in bytes. Picture an agent marketplace docking at a coastal inlet where every new operator must post a ferrous collateral bond — escrowed hardware attested to a real machine — before it can trade. Cloning an agent means duplicating that bond, so mass fake identities get expensive fast. Like a willow bending but holding, honest operators keep flexibility because their stake returns when they behave, while sybils forfeit theirs on slash — attack economics simply stop penciling out.
